A rule for scoring an arm's output

Source: R/core-bench-scorer.R
hr_scorer.Rd

A scorer is a function fn(item, output, label) that hr_benchmark() calls once per run of an arm on an item. item is the item's payload, output what the arm returned, and label the item's label from hr_reference(). It returns a list of

correct

TRUE, FALSE, or NA when the item cannot be scored (it has no label).

outcome

What the scorer saw, as one string (for the exact scorer, the answer as compared), or NA.

failure_kind

Why a wrong output was wrong: "parse_failure", "refusal", "not_in_document", "wrong", "budget_stop" or "error". NA when the output was correct.

A wrong output whose failure_kind is NA is recorded as "wrong". An output with a failure_kind is counted wrong, so a correct of NA beside one is recorded as FALSE, and TRUE beside one is an error in the scorer. The exception is an item with no label: every run on it is recorded NA, with its failure_kind kept.

Usage

hr_scorer(fn, name)

hr_scorer_exact(normalise = TRUE)

Arguments

fn

A function of (item, output, label) returning the list above.

name

The scorer's name, one string; it is recorded with the benchmark.

normalise

TRUE to fold case and white space before comparing.

Value

An object of class hr_scorer: a list of name and fn.

Details

hr_scorer_exact() compares the output's text with the label, and is the default scorer. The text is output itself when it is one string, or its answer or text element when it is a list (a gr_result has text). A label may hold several accepted answers; matching any one is correct. A number in a label is compared as written in plain digits, so the label 100000 accepts "100000" (not "1e+05"). With normalise = TRUE both sides are folded first: lower case, white space trimmed and runs of it collapsed to one space. Before comparing, it sorts out the outputs that are not answers:

  • an output with a failure_kind element from the list above is wrong for that reason, so an arm can report a refusal or a parse failure itself;

  • a gr_result with ok = FALSE is an "error";

  • no text at all (NULL, NA, an empty string, something with no answer or text) is a "parse_failure";

  • the text NOT_IN_DOCUMENT (in any case) is "not_in_document" unless the label accepts it.

See also

hr_benchmark()

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_qa_reference(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_mdd(), hr_reference(), hr_report()

Examples

exact <- hr_scorer_exact()
exact$fn("Capital of France?", "  paris ", "Paris")
#> $correct
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $outcome
#> [1] "paris"
#> 
#> $failure_kind
#> [1] NA
#> 
exact$fn("Capital of France?", "Lyon", "Paris")$failure_kind
#> [1] "wrong"

# A scorer of your own: a number within 1% of the label.
near <- hr_scorer(function(item, output, label) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(output))
  if (is.na(x)) return(list(correct = FALSE, outcome = NA, failure_kind = "parse_failure"))
  list(correct = abs(x - label) <= 0.01 * abs(label), outcome = format(x),
       failure_kind = NA)
}, name = "within_1pct")
near$fn(NULL, "45.3", 45.2)
#> $correct
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $outcome
#> [1] "45.3"
#> 
#> $failure_kind
#> [1] NA
#>
